title: Cohort transition matrix from issuer transitions
frame: DIKETAHUI: transitions (issuer, from, to) [n_obs] for one period, rating scale [R] with Default last. DITANYAKAN: counts N_ij, cohort sizes N_i, P_ij. RUMUS: card Core 1: P_ij = N_ij/N_i; default row absorbing; toolkit cohort_matrix(transitions, states, from_col, to_col). JAWAB: 1) map labels to scale. 2) crosstab counts in scale order (reindex missing states with 0). 3) N_i = row sums. 4) P = counts/N_i; empty origin -> identity row. 5) P[D] = e_D. 6) check rows sum 1.
pitfalls: empty origin row left as NaN

title: Cohort matrix with withdrawn / NR censoring
frame: DIKETAHUI: transitions including destination NR / WR / withdrawn. DITANYAKAN: NR-adjusted matrix. RUMUS: card V1 default (a): drop NR destinations from numerator AND denominator: P_ij = N_ij/(N_i - N_i,NR). JAWAB: 1) normalise labels (strip whitespace, case). 2) flag withdrawn codes (NR, WR, WD, withdrawn). 3) remove those rows. 4) recompute counts and N_i. 5) P. 6) check rows sum 1, no NR column.
pitfalls: keeping withdrawn issuers in the denominator understates every probability

title: Cohort matrix with NR kept as a state
frame: DIKETAHUI: transitions with NR destinations; task says keep NR as a state / report withdrawal rate. DITANYAKAN: matrix with an NR column (and NR row if NR can re-enter). RUMUS: card V1 (b): P_ij = N_ij/N_i with N_i including NR exits; NR column = withdrawal rate. JAWAB: 1) scale = ratings + D + NR in stated order. 2) counts. 3) divide by full N_i. 4) NR row absorbing unless data shows re-rating. 5) check rows sum 1 including NR.

title: NR redistribution pro rata
frame: DIKETAHUI: published percent matrix with an NR column [R x (R+1)]. DITANYAKAN: NR-free matrix. RUMUS: card V1 (c): P'_ij = P_ij/(1 - P_i,NR) (pro-rata over non-NR destinations), which equals removing NR from the denominator. JAWAB: 1) percent -> decimal. 2) extract NR column. 3) divide remaining cells by (1 - P_NR). 4) drop NR column. 5) check rows sum 1 (atol on unrounded data; published rounding can leave ~1e-3).
pitfalls: dividing by 100 after renormalising rows (order irrelevant, but not twice)

title: Percent matrix to probability matrix and orientation check
deliverables: matrix [R x R] probabilities, rows = from
frame: DIKETAHUI: matrix file in percent, header like BOP\EOP, possibly transposed. DITANYAKAN: probability matrix rows = from. RUMUS: card conventions: row sums ~100 -> divide by 100; if column sums ~1 and row sums not -> transpose. JAWAB: 1) parse (semicolon/latin-1 tolerant), strip labels. 2) compute row and column sums. 3) scale. 4) transpose if needed. 5) reorder to rating scale. 6) check rows sum 1, D row = e_D (add if missing).
pitfalls: checking row sums on rounded output with too tight atol

title: S&P notched ratings mapped to 7+1 scale
frame: DIKETAHUI: S&P ratings with notches (AA+, BBB-, CCC+, CC, C, SD, D). DITANYAKAN: mapped labels and matrix on AAA, AA, A, BBB, BB, B, CCC, D. RUMUS: card conventions / V6 (a): strip +/-; CCC+..C -> CCC; SD, D -> D. JAWAB: 1) uppercase and strip whitespace. 2) map per rule (dict + regex). 3) apply SAME map to every auxiliary file. 4) recompute counts and matrix on mapped scale. 5) check no unmapped labels remain.
pitfalls: mapping SD to CCC instead of default

title: Moody's ratings mapped to letter scale
frame: DIKETAHUI: Moody's ratings (Aaa, Aa1..Aa3, A1..A3, Baa1..Baa3, Ba1..Ba3, B1..B3, Caa1..Caa3, Ca, C, D/LD). DITANYAKAN: mapped scale matrix comparable to S&P. RUMUS: card conventions: Aaa->AAA, Aa*->AA, A*->A, Baa*->BBB, Ba*->BB, B*->B, Caa*/Ca/C->CCC, D/LD->D. JAWAB: 1) regex on prefix (check Baa before B, Aa before A). 2) map. 3) counts and P. 4) check labels exhausted.
pitfalls: prefix test order: 'B' matches 'Ba' and 'Baa'

title: Pooled multi-year cohort matrix (issuer-weighted)
deliverables: optional: mean of annual matrices for comparison
frame: DIKETAHUI: annual count matrices N_ij(t) [T x R x R] or transitions with cohort year. DITANYAKAN: pooled average matrix. RUMUS: card Core 1: P_bar_ij = sum_t N_ij(t) / sum_t N_i(t); NOT mean_t P_ij(t). JAWAB: 1) counts per year. 2) sum counts across years. 3) divide by summed row totals. 4) if asked, simple average of annual P for contrast. 5) check rows sum 1.
pitfalls: averaging annual P matrices (equal-year weights)

title: Multi-year transition matrix by matrix power
deliverables: matrix [R x R] for each horizon h
frame: DIKETAHUI: annual P [R x R], horizons h [H] (integers). DITANYAKAN: P(h). RUMUS: card Core 3: P(h) = P^h (np.linalg.matrix_power); toolkit matrix_power_migration(P, years). Non-integer h: expm(h logm P) with DA fix. JAWAB: 1) normalise P. 2) power per horizon. 3) check rows sum 1, D row absorbing, PD column non-decreasing in h.
pitfalls: elementwise power P**h instead of matrix power

title: Cumulative default probability term structure by rating
deliverables: table [R x H]: cumulative PD (probability or percent)
frame: DIKETAHUI: annual P, horizons [H]. DITANYAKAN: PD_i(h) for each non-default rating. RUMUS: card Core 3: PD_i(h) = [P^h]_{i,D}; toolkit cumulative_default_probs(P, horizons). JAWAB: 1) powers. 2) take D column. 3) drop D row (or keep 1). 4) percent if asked. 5) check PD(1) = P[:,D], non-decreasing in h, -> 1 if D reachable.

title: Marginal and conditional (forward) default probabilities
deliverables: table [R x H]: cumulative, marginal, conditional PD
frame: DIKETAHUI: cumulative PD_i(h) [R x H] (or P to compute it). DITANYAKAN: marginal and conditional PDs. RUMUS: card Core 3: marginal(h) = PD(h) - PD(h-1); conditional(h) = (PD(h)-PD(h-1))/(1-PD(h-1)), PD(0) = 0. JAWAB: 1) cumulative. 2) diff along horizon with PD(0)=0. 3) divide by survival. 4) check marginals sum to PD(H), conditional in [0,1].
pitfalls: horizons not consecutive: marginal between listed horizons, say so

title: Average annualised default rate from cumulative PD
deliverables: table [R x H]: average annual PD
frame: DIKETAHUI: cumulative PD_i(h). DITANYAKAN: average annual PD. RUMUS: card Core 3: a(h) = 1 - (1 - PD(h))^(1/h); simple alternative PD(h)/h only if stated. JAWAB: 1) cumulative PDs. 2) survival 1-PD. 3) power 1/h. 4) a = 1 - that. 5) check a(1) = PD(1); a <= PD(h).

title: Generator matrix from annual matrix (logm with diagonal adjustment)
deliverables: matrix [R x R] generator Q (per year)
frame: DIKETAHUI: annual P. DITANYAKAN: valid generator Q. RUMUS: card Core 4: Q0 = real(scipy.linalg.logm(P)); DA: set negative off-diagonals to 0, then q_ii = -sum_{j!=i} q_ij; Q[D] = 0; toolkit generator_from_matrix(P, fix='DA'). JAWAB: 1) logm, take .real. 2) record negatives. 3) clip off-diagonals BEFORE resetting diagonal. 4) default row 0. 5) check rows sum 0, off-diag >= 0, expm(Q) ~ P.
pitfalls: setting the diagonal before clipping negatives

title: Generator with weighted adjustment (WA)
deliverables: comparison: ||expm(Q) - P|| for DA and WA
frame: DIKETAHUI: annual P. DITANYAKAN: Q via weighted adjustment and fit vs DA. RUMUS: card Core 4: zero negative off-diagonals; row excess e_i = sum_j q_ij (after zeroing, should be 0); subtract e_i |q_ij| / sum_k |q_ik| from each entry (diagonal included); Q[D] = 0. JAWAB: 1) logm real. 2) G = |Q0| row sums. 3) zero negatives. 4) redistribute row excess proportionally. 5) check rows sum 0, off-diag >= 0. 6) compare Frobenius error of expm(Q) - P.
pitfalls: weights from the clipped rather than original |q_ij|: follow the stated source

title: Embeddability diagnostics of a transition matrix
deliverables: summary: det(P), min diagonal, negative entries list, embeddable flag
frame: DIKETAHUI: P. DITANYAKAN: whether an exact valid generator exists and diagnostics. RUMUS: card Core 4 pitfalls: det(P) <= 0 or diagonal < 0.5 -> log may not exist/unique; embeddable iff real logm has q_ij >= 0 off-diagonal and rows sum 0. JAWAB: 1) det. 2) min diagonal. 3) eigenvalues (negative real -> no real log). 4) logm and list negative off-diagonals (from->to). 5) report flag; still apply DA if asked.

title: Duration (continuous-time) estimator from rating histories
frame: DIKETAHUI: rating spells per issuer (state, start date, end date, exit state or censor) over window [0,T]. DITANYAKAN: Q and P(1). RUMUS: card Core 2: q_ij = N_ij(0,T)/int Y_i ds; q_ii = -sum q_ij; P(t) = expm(Qt). JAWAB: 1) clip spells to window. 2) exposure years per state (ACT/365.25). 3) count i->j transitions. 4) divide. 5) Q[D]=0. 6) expm. 7) check rows of P sum 1, AAA PD > 0 if paths exist.
pitfalls: counting withdrawal as a transition (it is censoring)

title: Fractional-horizon matrices from the generator
deliverables: matrix [R x R] for each fractional t
frame: DIKETAHUI: Q (or annual P to derive Q), horizons t [K] in years (e.g. 0.25, 0.5). DITANYAKAN: P(t). RUMUS: card Core 4 conventions: Q from 1-year P is per year; P(t) = scipy.linalg.expm(t Q). JAWAB: 1) Q with DA. 2) expm per t. 3) clip tiny negatives to 0 and renormalise only if task says. 4) check P(1) ~ input P, rows sum 1, P(t1) P(t2) = P(t1+t2).
pitfalls: using P**t elementwise or P^0.25 by fractional matrix_power without fix

title: Cohort vs duration estimates of high-grade default probability
deliverables: table [R]: PD cohort, PD duration, difference
frame: DIKETAHUI: rating histories (dated). DITANYAKAN: one-year PD by rating under both estimators. RUMUS: card Core 1 vs 2: cohort gives exactly 0 where no default observed; duration expm(Q) gives positive PD via intermediate paths. JAWAB: 1) annual cohort snapshots -> P_cohort. 2) spells -> Q -> P_dur. 3) D columns. 4) differences. 5) check both rows sum 1; duration PD(AAA) > 0 if any downgrade path observed.

title: Time-homogeneity chi-squared test across cohorts
deliverables: table [R origins]: X2, df, p_value, reject
frame: DIKETAHUI: count matrices per cohort year [T x R x R], alpha, sparsity filter. DITANYAKAN: per-origin X2, df, p, reject. RUMUS: card Core 5: for origin i table O [cohorts x destinations]; E_tj = R_t K_j/N; X2 = sum (O-E)^2/E; df = (r-1)(k-1); p = chi2.sf. JAWAB: 1) build table. 2) drop zero-issuer cohorts; apply filter to column totals. 3) if < 2 rows or cols: stat 0, df 0, p 1. 4) compute manually (no Yates). 5) reject = p < alpha.
pitfalls: chi2_contingency Yates correction when df == 1

title: Likelihood-ratio (G2) homogeneity test
frame: DIKETAHUI: per-origin contingency tables (cohorts x destinations). DITANYAKAN: G2 statistic and p. RUMUS: card Core 5: G2 = 2 sum O ln(O/E) over cells with O > 0; df = (r-1)(k-1); p = chi2.sf(G2, df). JAWAB: 1) expected counts. 2) sum over O > 0 (0 ln 0 = 0). 3) df after filtering. 4) p, reject. 5) degenerate table -> 0, 0, 1.

title: Markov property test: dependence on previous move (momentum)
deliverables: table: transition probabilities by prior move
frame: DIKETAHUI: rating histories with at least three consecutive snapshots. DITANYAKAN: does next-period transition from i depend on whether issuer was downgraded / upgraded / stable into i? RUMUS: per origin i: contingency table [prior-move groups x destinations]; Pearson X2 as card Core 5, df = (g-1)(k-1). JAWAB: 1) build triples (prev, cur, next). 2) group by cur and prior move. 3) tables, filter sparse columns. 4) X2, p. 5) report downgrade-momentum probabilities.
formulas: P(next | cur, prior move) = N / N_group

title: Clopper-Pearson exact confidence interval for default rates
deliverables: table [R]: defaults, issuers, rate, lower, upper
frame: DIKETAHUI: defaults x_i and cohort sizes n_i per rating, alpha. DITANYAKAN: two-sided CI per rating. RUMUS: card Core 6: lo = Beta.ppf(a/2, x, n-x+1), hi = Beta.ppf(1-a/2, x+1, n-x); x = 0 -> lo = 0, hi = 1 - (a/2)^(1/n); x = n -> hi = 1. JAWAB: 1) counts. 2) scipy.stats.beta.ppf with edge cases. 3) report percent if asked. 4) check lo <= p_hat <= hi.
pitfalls: Beta.ppf with parameter 0 returns NaN: handle x=0 and x=n

title: Wald and Wilson intervals for transition probabilities
deliverables: table [R x R]: p, se, lower, upper
frame: DIKETAHUI: counts N_ij, N_i, confidence level. DITANYAKAN: CI per cell. RUMUS: card Core 6: Wald p +/- z sqrt(p(1-p)/n); Wilson: (p + z^2/(2n) +/- z sqrt(p(1-p)/n + z^2/(4n^2)))/(1 + z^2/n). JAWAB: 1) p_ij. 2) z = Phi^-1(1-a/2). 3) chosen interval. 4) clip Wald to [0,1]. 5) check Wilson nonzero width at p = 0.

title: Rule of three upper bound with zero observed defaults
deliverables: table [R]: n, upper bound exact, rule-of-three approx
frame: DIKETAHUI: cohort sizes n_i with zero defaults, confidence level c. DITANYAKAN: one-sided upper PD bound. RUMUS: card Core 6: exact one-sided: 1 - (1-c)^(1/n); approx 3/n at 95%; two-sided Clopper-Pearson hi at a/2 differs. JAWAB: 1) n. 2) exact bound. 3) approximation. 4) report which side. 5) check bound decreasing in n.
pitfalls: using two-sided alpha/2 when one-sided is asked

title: Investment-grade vs speculative-grade aggregate default rates
deliverables: table: IG, SG, all: defaults, issuers, default rate
frame: DIKETAHUI: counts by rating (issuers, defaults) per cohort year. DITANYAKAN: aggregate IG, SG and all-rated default rates. RUMUS: card V4 (a): rate = sum defaults / sum issuers within group (issuer-weighted); IG = AAA..BBB, SG = BB..CCC. JAWAB: 1) map ratings to group. 2) sum defaults and issuers. 3) divide. 4) per-year then pooled if asked. 5) check SG rate >= IG rate typically; not mean of rating PDs.
formulas: DR_group = sum_{i in group} D_i / sum_{i in group} N_i
pitfalls: simple average of rating-level rates

title: Volume-weighted (exposure-weighted) default rate
deliverables: table: issuer-weighted vs volume-weighted rate per group
frame: DIKETAHUI: issuers with rating, default flag, debt amount. DITANYAKAN: volume-weighted default rates. RUMUS: card V4 (b): DR_vol = sum amount_defaulted / sum amount_rated. JAWAB: 1) group. 2) sums of amounts. 3) ratio. 4) compare with issuer-weighted. 5) check in [0,1].

title: Annual default rate time series statistics by rating
frame: DIKETAHUI: per year and rating: issuers and defaults (or transitions with year). DITANYAKAN: annual rates, mean (simple and issuer-weighted), std ddof=1. RUMUS: DR_t = D_t/N_t; simple mean = mean_t DR_t; weighted = sum D_t / sum N_t. JAWAB: 1) table per year. 2) rates (skip N_t = 0). 3) stats. 4) state which mean. 5) check weighted mean between min and max.
formulas: weighted mean = sum_t D_t / sum_t N_t

title: Empirical static-pool cumulative default rates vs Markov
deliverables: table [R x H]: empirical cumulative, Markov cumulative, difference
frame: DIKETAHUI: issuer rating histories with annual snapshots, horizons [H]. DITANYAKAN: empirical cumulative PD (static pools by start rating) vs P^h. RUMUS: card V5 (b): empirical PD_i(h) = defaults by h among cohort rated i at t0 / cohort size (withdrawn removed per stated rule); (a): [P^h]_{iD}. JAWAB: 1) cohorts per start year. 2) follow h years. 3) pool across start years (issuer-weighted). 4) compute P^h. 5) differences.
pitfalls: withdrawn issuers handled differently in the two measures

title: Hidden defaults completion from a default-rate table
deliverables: matrix [R x R] completed counts and probabilities
frame: DIKETAHUI: visible transition counts [R x R] and a separate true default-count table by rating [R]. DITANYAKAN: reconciled matrix. RUMUS: card completing: hidden_i = max(true_D_i - visible_D_i, 0); add to D cell; N_i grows by hidden_i; P = counts/N_i. JAWAB: 1) map ratings in both files with same map. 2) compute hidden. 3) add to D column. 4) recompute rows. 5) check D column now equals true defaults.

title: Counts reconstruction from percentages and cohort sizes
frame: DIKETAHUI: percent matrices and cohort sizes N_i (per year). DITANYAKAN: counts for pooling or testing. RUMUS: card completing: N_ij = round(pct_ij/100 N_i). JAWAB: 1) parse. 2) multiply. 3) round to integers. 4) row sums may differ from N_i by rounding: report. 5) use counts in pooled or chi-squared steps.

title: Upgrade, downgrade, stay and default partition per rating
deliverables: table [R]: p_up, p_stay, p_down, p_default, drift
frame: DIKETAHUI: P [R x R] best->worst, D last. DITANYAKAN: probability partition and drift. RUMUS: card invariant: up = sum_{j<i} P_ij; stay = P_ii; down = sum_{i<j<D} P_ij (excluding default); default = P_iD; drift = sum_j P_ij (j - i) (notches). JAWAB: 1) index order. 2) sums. 3) drift. 4) check up + stay + down + default = 1.
pitfalls: counting default as a downgrade

title: Mobility indices of a transition matrix
deliverables: summary: Shorrocks trace index, eigenvalue index, SVD metric
frame: DIKETAHUI: P [R x R]. DITANYAKAN: mobility indices. RUMUS: Shorrocks M_T = (R - trace P)/(R - 1); determinant index 1 - |det P|^(1/(R-1)); Jafry-Schuermann M_SVD = mean of singular values of (P - I). JAWAB: 1) trace. 2) det. 3) SVD of P - I. 4) indices. 5) check identity matrix -> 0.

title: Distance between two transition matrices
deliverables: summary: L1, L2, max abs, SVD metric difference
frame: DIKETAHUI: two matrices P_A, P_B on possibly different scales/labels. DITANYAKAN: difference matrix and norms. RUMUS: card completing: add missing columns as 0, reorder to target scale; D = P_A - P_B; ||D||_1 (mean absolute or sum as stated), Frobenius, max abs; M_SVD(P_A) - M_SVD(P_B). JAWAB: 1) harmonise labels. 2) align. 3) diff. 4) norms. 5) argmax cell label 'FROM->TO' (first in row-major on ties).

title: Rating distribution evolution of a portfolio
deliverables: table [H x R]: distribution per horizon
frame: DIKETAHUI: initial counts or weights per rating pi_0 [R], P, horizons [H]. DITANYAKAN: distribution pi_h and expected defaulted share. RUMUS: pi_h = pi_0 P^h (row vector); expected defaults = N pi_h[D]. JAWAB: 1) normalise pi_0. 2) matrix power. 3) multiply. 4) expected counts. 5) check pi_h sums 1, pi_h[D] non-decreasing.
pitfalls: right-multiplying by column vector (uses P transposed)

title: Expected time to default via the fundamental matrix
frame: DIKETAHUI: annual P with D absorbing. DITANYAKAN: expected number of years until default from each rating. RUMUS: transient block T (non-default rows/cols); N = (I - T)^-1; t = N 1. JAWAB: 1) partition P. 2) solve linear system (I - T) t = 1. 3) report years. 4) check t positive, generally increasing with rating quality.
pitfalls: including D in the transient block makes I - T singular

title: Point-in-time conditional transition matrix (one-factor credit cycle)
deliverables: matrix [R x R] conditional on Z
frame: DIKETAHUI: TTC matrix P, asset correlation rho, cycle factor Z. DITANYAKAN: conditional matrix P(Z). RUMUS: thresholds per row from worst cumulative: x_ik = Phi^-1(sum_{j>=k} P_ij); P_ik(Z) = Phi((x_ik - sqrt(rho)Z)/sqrt(1-rho)) - Phi((x_i,k+1 - sqrt(rho)Z)/sqrt(1-rho)). JAWAB: 1) thresholds (clip at +/-inf). 2) shifted CDF differences. 3) D row absorbing. 4) check rows sum 1, Z < 0 raises downgrades and defaults, Z = 0 not equal to P unless rho = 0.
formulas: P_ik(Z) = Phi((x_ik - sqrt(rho) Z)/sqrt(1-rho)) - Phi((x_i,k+1 - sqrt(rho) Z)/sqrt(1-rho))

title: Calibrating the credit-cycle index to an observed year
frame: DIKETAHUI: TTC matrix, rho, observed annual counts N_ij(t). DITANYAKAN: Z_t that best fits year t. RUMUS: P(Z) as in the conditional-matrix frame; minimise weighted SSE sum_ij N_i (P_ij(t) - P_ij(Z))^2 / (P_ij(Z)(1-P_ij(Z))) or maximise multinomial log-likelihood sum N_ij ln P_ij(Z). JAWAB: 1) build P(Z). 2) objective. 3) scipy.optimize.minimize_scalar on [-5, 5]. 4) report Z, fit. 5) check bad years Z < 0.

title: Jarrow-Lando-Turnbull risk-neutral transition matrix
frame: DIKETAHUI: physical one-year P, risky zero prices per rating B_i(0,1), risk-free P(0,1), recovery delta. DITANYAKAN: risk-neutral matrix. RUMUS: JLT 1997: risk-neutral default prob q_iD = (1 - B_i/P(0,1))/(1-delta); pi_i = q_iD/P_iD; q_ij = pi_i P_ij (j != i), q_ii = 1 - sum_{j!=i} q_ij. JAWAB: 1) q_iD from prices. 2) pi_i. 3) scale off-diagonals. 4) check q_ii >= 0, rows sum 1.
pitfalls: P_iD = 0 for top grades makes pi undefined: report

title: Cleaning a published matrix: rounding, negatives, renormalisation
frame: DIKETAHUI: published matrix (rounded percents, row sums off). DITANYAKAN: valid stochastic matrix. RUMUS: P = clip(M/100, 0, 1); P_i = P_i / sum_j P_ij; D row = e_D. JAWAB: 1) parse. 2) record deviations. 3) clip. 4) renormalise rows (only if task permits). 5) check rows sum 1 atol 1e-9 on unrounded data; do not round before checks.
pitfalls: tight row-sum check on 6-dp rounded output fails by ~n*5e-7

title: Coarse-state lumping (IG / SG / D) of a transition matrix
frame: DIKETAHUI: fine counts N_ij or P with cohort sizes N_i. DITANYAKAN: coarse matrix. RUMUS: from counts: P_GH = sum_{i in G, j in H} N_ij / sum_{i in G} N_i (issuer-weighted). JAWAB: 1) group map. 2) sum counts block-wise. 3) divide. 4) without counts: weight rows by stated distribution. 5) check rows sum 1.
formulas: P_GH = sum_{i in G} sum_{j in H} N_ij / sum_{i in G} N_i
pitfalls: unweighted average of fine rows

title: Cross-agency comparison on a common scale
frame: DIKETAHUI: matrices from two agencies with different label sets. DITANYAKAN: harmonised comparison. RUMUS: card conventions: map both to 7+1 (Moody's Baa->BBB etc.); missing destinations as 0; reorder. JAWAB: 1) map labels. 2) aggregate notches by counts if available, else by given weights. 3) align. 4) differences in D column and diagonals. 5) check each matrix rows sum 1.

title: Duration estimator with censoring at withdrawal
frame: DIKETAHUI: rating action history with dates, withdrawal dates, observation window end. DITANYAKAN: Q. RUMUS: card Core 2: exposure for state i accumulates until next action, withdrawal or window end; withdrawals are censoring (no transition); q_ij = N_ij / exposure_i. JAWAB: 1) sort actions per issuer. 2) build spells. 3) truncate at withdrawal / window. 4) exposures in years. 5) counts of i->j. 6) Q, DA not needed (valid by construction). 7) check rows sum 0.
formulas: exposure_i = sum spells length in state i

title: Direct multi-year cohort matrix vs P^h (Markov check)
frame: DIKETAHUI: snapshots h years apart and annual transitions. DITANYAKAN: direct h-year cohort matrix vs annual P raised to h. RUMUS: direct: P^(h)_ij = N_ij(0,h)/N_i(0); Markov: P^h. JAWAB: 1) h-year pairs (start rating, rating at t0+h, withdrawn removed). 2) direct matrix. 3) annual pooled P. 4) power. 5) differences and default column comparison.

title: Bootstrap confidence intervals for transition probabilities
deliverables: table [R]: PD estimate, bootstrap SE, CI
frame: DIKETAHUI: issuer-level transitions, B replications, seed, level. DITANYAKAN: bootstrap CI for P_ij (e.g. default column). RUMUS: resample issuers with replacement (rng = default_rng(seed)), recompute cohort P each replicate; percentile CI = quantiles at a/2, 1-a/2; SE = std(ddof=1). JAWAB: 1) issuer ids. 2) B resamples. 3) matrices. 4) stats. 5) check CI contains point estimate.

title: Quarterly to annual matrix and annual to quarterly root
deliverables: matrix [R x R] annual from quarterly, or quarterly from annual
frame: DIKETAHUI: quarterly P_q or annual P. DITANYAKAN: the other frequency. RUMUS: annual = P_q^4; quarterly = expm(0.25 Q), Q = DA-fixed logm(P) (card Core 4); alternative scipy.linalg.fractional_matrix_power with negative-entry fix. JAWAB: 1) choose direction. 2) compute. 3) clip and report negatives if root used. 4) check rows sum 1, round-trip error.

title: Most likely destination per origin and largest migrations
frame: DIKETAHUI: P. DITANYAKAN: argmax destination per origin, largest off-diagonal migrations. RUMUS: card pitfalls: ties -> first occurrence in row-major order; label 'FROM->TO'. JAWAB: 1) np.argmax per row. 2) mask diagonal for off-diagonal ranking. 3) sort descending (stable). 4) labels. 5) check probabilities match P.

title: Accuracy ratio / Gini of a rating scale
frame: DIKETAHUI: issuers with rating at cohort start and default flag within horizon. DITANYAKAN: AUC, accuracy ratio. RUMUS: order ratings worst->best; AUC = P(score_D worse than score_ND) + 0.5 P(tie); AR = 2 AUC - 1. JAWAB: 1) rating rank numeric (worse = higher risk). 2) counts by rating of defaulters and survivors. 3) AUC via Mann-Whitney with ties. 4) AR. 5) check in [-1,1].

title: Expected loss by rating bucket using matrix PDs
frame: DIKETAHUI: P, exposures by rating (EAD), LGD, horizon h. DITANYAKAN: EL per bucket and total. RUMUS: PD_i(h) = [P^h]_{iD}; EL_i = PD_i LGD EAD_i. JAWAB: 1) cumulative PDs. 2) join exposures by mapped rating. 3) EL. 4) sum. 5) check EL monotone with PD across buckets.

title: Annual snapshot cohorts from dated rating actions
deliverables: transitions table [n_obs]: issuer, year, from, to
frame: DIKETAHUI: rating action history (issuer, date, new rating), cohort dates. DITANYAKAN: one-period transitions and cohort matrix. RUMUS: rating at date t = last action on or before t (merge_asof); from = rating at t, to = rating at t+1; default at any time inside period -> to = D (default dominates later re-rating). JAWAB: 1) sort, parse dates. 2) snapshots. 3) pairs. 4) drop unrated at start; censor withdrawn. 5) card Core 1.
formulas: rating(t) = last action with date <= t
pitfalls: missing intra-year default that was followed by a re-rating

title: Survival and hazard by rating from the generator
frame: DIKETAHUI: Q (or annual P), time grid [K]. DITANYAKAN: S_i(t) = 1 - PD_i(t) and hazard h_i(t) = -d ln S_i/dt. RUMUS: PD_i(t) = [expm(tQ)]_{iD}; hazard via finite difference of -ln S; at t -> 0 hazard = q_iD. JAWAB: 1) expm per t. 2) S. 3) log-diff hazard. 4) check S decreasing, h(0) ~ q_iD.

title: Goodness-of-fit of observed transitions to a reference matrix
frame: DIKETAHUI: observed counts N_ij for a year, reference matrix P0. DITANYAKAN: per-row test that row i follows P0_i. RUMUS: X2_i = sum_j (N_ij - N_i P0_ij)^2/(N_i P0_ij) over cells with P0_ij > 0; df = (#cells) - 1; p = chi2.sf; overall: sum X2_i, sum df. JAWAB: 1) align scales. 2) expected counts. 3) exclude zero-expected cells (observed there -> report). 4) stats, p. 5) reject at alpha.

title: Default row and missing states fix before computation
frame: DIKETAHUI: matrix without default row, or missing destination columns, or states in non-scale order. DITANYAKAN: complete square matrix on target scale. RUMUS: card conventions: add missing columns as 0; add D row = e_D; reorder rows and columns to scale; empty origin -> identity row. JAWAB: 1) reindex rows/cols to scale with fill 0. 2) D row. 3) empty rows -> identity. 4) check square, rows sum 1, Q later has D row 0.

title: Default rate by rating with confidence bands over cohort years
deliverables: table [R]: pooled PD, CI, number of years with defaults
frame: DIKETAHUI: per year x rating issuers and defaults. DITANYAKAN: pooled PD per rating with CI and dispersion. RUMUS: pooled PD_i = sum_t D_it / sum_t N_it (issuer-weighted); Clopper-Pearson CI on pooled counts (card Core 6). JAWAB: 1) pool. 2) CI. 3) count years with D > 0. 4) check monotonic tendency but do not force monotonicity.
pitfalls: forcing grade monotonicity by smoothing when not asked
